title: CVE-2022-42915: HTTP proxy double-free
excerpt:
This is a finding that Trail of Bits found in their ongoing curl security audit. Reported at a status meeting today.

## Summary:

curl frees memory twice in some cleanup function related to HTTP proxies.

It as simple as `curl -x http://localhost:80 dict://127.0.0.1`

Using valgrind on the current git master, it shows:

summary: curl frees memory twice in some cleanup function related to HTTP proxies.

claims.text: curl frees memory twice in some cleanup function related to HTTP proxies
claims.reasoning: The code shows two distinct free paths for the same memory block allocated in connect_init: first via Curl_free_request_state freeing data->req.p.http (which points to a struct member), then via conn_free freeing conn->connect_state (the original allocation pointer).

citations.note: Curl_free_request_state calls Curl_safefree(data->req.p.http) which points into the http_connect_state allocation during proxy CONNECT
conn_free calls Curl_safefree(conn->connect_state) freeing the original allocation
connect_init allocates http_connect_state with calloc and stores in conn->connect_state
data->req.p.http = &s->http_proxy makes req.p.http point into the middle of the allocation

claims.text: the double free occurs in cleanup functions of the HTTP proxy handling code
claims.reasoning: Both free sites are in cleanup functions (Curl_free_request_state and conn_free) and the allocation occurs in HTTP proxy handling code (connect_init).

citations.note: Curl_free_request_state is a cleanup function called from Curl_close
conn_free is called from Curl_disconnect during connection cleanup
connect_init is the HTTP proxy CONNECT initialization function

claims.text: using a proxy URL with dict:// scheme, e.g. `curl -x http://localhost:80 dict://127.0.0.1`
claims.reasoning: Using a non-HTTP protocol (dict://) over an HTTP proxy triggers the proxy CONNECT path in connect_init, which performs the problematic pointer swap and allocation.

citations.note: connect_init checks PROTOPT_NOTCPPROXY flag - dict protocol would not have this flag
Allocation occurs when reinit is false, which happens for the initial proxy CONNECT

claims.reasoning: The valgrind output provided in the report shows an invalid free (freeing a non-malloc pointer) followed by a second free of the same memory block, which is a classic double-free leading to memory corruption.

citations.note: curl_dbg_free calls the real free function on the pointer
Valgrind output shows 'Invalid free()' at this location for the first free

claims.text: run curl with valgrind on the command `curl -x http://localhost:80 dict://127.0.0.1` to see the invalid free
claims.reasoning: The valgrind output in the report directly demonstrates the reproduction steps with the exact command provided.

citations.note: Valgrind output shows allocation at connect_init (http_proxy.c:174) triggered by the reported command

key_reasons: The code at lib/http_proxy.c:174 allocates http_connect_state and stores it in conn->connect_state
At lib/http_proxy.c:191, data->req.p.http is set to point to a struct member (&s->http_proxy) inside that allocation
Curl_free_request_state at lib/url.c:2259 calls Curl_safefree(data->req.p.http), freeing the struct member pointer (invalid free)
conn_free at lib/url.c:810 calls Curl_safefree(conn->connect_state), freeing the original allocation pointer (double-free)
The valgrind output confirms both frees occur on the same 984-byte block
The trigger (non-HTTP protocol over HTTP proxy) is a valid user-controlled input
reply: Thank you for this detailed report. The double-free is confirmed: connect_init (http_proxy.c:174) allocates http_connect_state, then line 191 makes data->req.p.http point into that struct. Curl_free_request_state (url.c:2259) incorrectly frees that interior pointer, and conn_free (url.c:810) later frees the original allocation. This is reachable via `curl -x http://proxy dict://target` as you demonstrated. We'll fix this promptly.
